content.text:
Typecheck, lint, and the tests touching these files all pass. Here's what changed and the answer to your third question.

## 1 & 2 — done

**Type scale, all four panels** (`src/global.css`, one new `.board-panel` block; applied in `src/routes/editor/index.tsx:1171`). Every panel body rendered through `.comment-markdown` — persona notes, margin comments, source notes, the rubric review — now sits at **14px/1.6** instead of the 12–13.6px each panel had picked for itself. Typewriter chrome has a hard floor of 11px, so nothing in Cast/Marginalia/Apparatus renders at 9.6px any more.

**Rubric panel restructure** (`src/components/rubric/rubric-panel.tsx`):

- **One long scroll → three short ones.** The verdict (grade, score, summary, trend) is pinned at the top; below it a segmented control switches between **Marks / The Room / Review**. Re-read and Full report are pinned at the bottom instead of buried a few thousand pixels down.
- **Criteria are rows, not cards.** All eleven fit on one screen as label + bar + mark. The reasoning paragraph and the "Next move" line — your "three descriptions for one thing" — open on click, at 14px. Header no longer repeats the brief summary (that moved to the empty state).
- **The judges got a real interface.** They were a bulleted list keyed by *raw persona id* (`devil`, `scholar`) in 12px italic, with the model's Markdown flattened to plain text — that's why the quotes vanished. Each is now a card: portrait icon, actual name, role, colour-matched to the Cast, score chip, and the rationale rendered as Markdown so quoted passages and emphasis survive.

I haven't run it in the browser — say the word and I'll launch it and screenshot.

## 3 — the buttons

There are actually **four** in the Cast panel, and the useful distinction is *what comes back*:

| Button | What it does | What you get |
|---|---|---|
| **✦ Convene the Room** | All five editors read the whole draft, each files **one short note** anchored to a quoted sentence | Notes in the feed + pins in the manuscript, each repliable. **Never touches your text.** |
| **❡ Expand to full analysis** | Each editor writes a **full-page memo**, then a synthesis ("The Room's Verdict") | A long report in a modal, downloadable as Markdown. No anchors, no replies. |
| **✎ Mark up my draft** | Picks anchor sentences deterministically (longest one for the Copy Chief, an unsupported-claim sentence for the Devil's Advocate, an evidence sentence for the Scholar), asks each editor to **rewrite** that passage | **Actual proposed edits** to your prose, as accept/reject changes, budget-bounded |
| **Strike the room** | Clears the feed, the inline pins, and local storage | Nothing — it's a delete |

So: **Convene = talk. Mark up = edit. Full analysis = essay. Strike = clear.**

Two things make this genuinely confusing, and they're real design problems, not just labelling:

1. **Convene and Full analysis are the same content at two lengths.** Same five editors, same draft, differing only in word count and destination. That's a depth setting wearing a button.
2. **Mark up is the only one that changes your writing** — and it's styled as the quietest of the three, below a dashed secondary. The one irreversible action looks the least important.

Also worth naming: the background room already reads as you write and leaves passing notes, so Convene is partly "do it now" rather than a distinct capability.

content.text:
All three are done. Typecheck, ESLint, and the touched test files pass.

## What changed

**Type scale — all four board panels** (`src/global.css`, `src/routes/editor/index.tsx:1171`)
A `.board-panel` block sets one floor for the whole editorial board: prose rendered through `.comment-markdown` (persona notes, margin comments, source notes, the rubric review) is now **14px/1.6** instead of the 12–13.6px each panel had chosen independently, and typewriter chrome bottoms out at 11px so nothing renders at 9.6px. One place, four panels.

**Rubric panel** (`src/components/rubric/rubric-panel.tsx`)
- One endless scroll became three short ones: the verdict pins to the top, a **Marks / The Room / Review** segmented control switches between them, and Re-read + Full report pin to the bottom.
- Criteria are now rows — all eleven visible at once as label + bar + mark. The reasoning paragraph and "Next move" line open on click, at readable size. That's the "three descriptions for one thing" collapsed to one that you ask for.
- The judges were the worst of it: a bulleted list keyed by raw persona id (`devil`, `scholar`) in 12px italic with the model's Markdown flattened to plain text — which is exactly why the quotes disappeared. Each is now a card with the editor's icon, real name, role, Cast-matching colour, a score chip, and the rationale rendered as Markdown.

**Cast panel** (`src/components/personas/personas-panel.tsx`)
Four buttons became two, split by what they do to your text:

- **✦ Read my draft** — filled, primary. "Five editors leave short notes in the margin. Your text is untouched."
- **✎ Edit my draft** — outlined. "The room proposes rewrites you accept or reject — up to N this pass." The one action that changes your prose no longer looks like the quietest thing on screen.
- **❡ full analysis ↗** — a small link beneath, since it's the same five editors at greater length.
- **Strike the room** moved out of the action row entirely into the notes-feed header as `clear ✕`, next to the note count and the grouped/compact toggles — it's a delete, not a third way to ask for something.

I also updated the two places that named the old buttons: the empty state at `/analysis`, and the per-feature model labels in Settings (now "Read My Draft (room notes)" / "Edit My Draft (rewrites)") so what you set there matches what you click.

I haven't run this in a browser — everything above is verified by typecheck, lint, and tests only. Want me to launch it and check the panels visually?
